rule-strong.note: Six-digit hex with an appended alpha byte (0x60 ≈ 38%).

provisional-ink.note: The text printed onto the ochre band, themed exactly as secure-ink is. 6.82:1 on provisional in light, 7.57:1 in dark; both pairs are asserted by lib/theme-contrast.test.ts.

display.purpose: One size, one place: the door headline on the auth surface. The world's only display setting.

designation.purpose: The room screen's one step of display scale and the only place the value voice is set large: the active room code in the header register, carrying the document's own identity. Deliberately the value voice rather than the Archivo display size, so enlarging a machine fact does not turn it into a headline.

title.purpose: The name on a credential and the operator in the bearer strip. Sentence case, normal width — never tracked caps.

body.purpose: Message text in the access register, rendered from a whitespace-preserving pre in the sans voice.

note.purpose: Running voice for asides, hints and status prose beside a legend. Where a sentence goes instead of a legend.

label.purpose: Every printed legend, column head, role band, badge and button face. Coloured via :where(.legend) at zero specificity.

mark.purpose: The smallest step, and a marking step rather than a reading step. Legal in exactly two places: a word stamped onto an object (the Owner only corner stamp on an overprinted field) and initials struck inside a credential mark (IdentityChip at 24px). Never legal on reading matter — anything a person reads starts at the 0.625rem legend.

value.purpose: Anything a machine produced: ids, tokens, room codes, timestamps, counts, file paths. Tabular figures, zero-padded counts.

mrz.purpose: The machine-readable strip only. Real payload characters, chevron-padded into 30-character courses, never case-normalised.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The resting shadow of an issued credential. Nothing else in the room carries it.

shadows.name: lift-high
shadows.purpose: Objects genuinely above the desk: toast slips and the mobile palette sheet.

motion.name: print-in
motion.purpose: A slip or pass that was just printed. Things print; they do not fade in.

motion.name: rail-in
motion.value: 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) — 10px from the left, 35ms stagger capped at the 6th item
motion.purpose: Credentials arriving on the rack rail.

motion.name: stamp-down
motion.purpose: The cancellation stamp landing on a revoked credential.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: The primary button under :active. Nothing scales up on hover.

motion.name: lamp-read
motion.purpose: The amber reading lamp. A hard blink, not a pulse — a reader LED does not breathe.

motion.name: reader-sweep
motion.value: 900ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite — a lamp-tinted gradient crossing the element
motion.purpose: The one authored moment. Runs only while something is genuinely being read: the agent streaming, or the session credential verifying on load. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: The room becomes a fixed-height three-column desk with internally scrolling columns. Below this it is a single stacked column with the register first.

verification.contrast: lib/theme-contrast.test.ts parses tokens out of app/globals.css and asserts 4.5:1 in both themes for every foreground/background pair that ships text, plus 3:1 for the lamp on the sheet. No shipped text pair is uncovered. Run: bun test.
capturedViewports: stacked layout via a temporary --breakpoint-lg override
unverified: Mobile was verified structurally by temporarily raising --breakpoint-lg, which covers column order, overflow and control clearance. Anything depending on real viewport width — tap targets, wrapping at 390px, the sheet against a soft keyboard, safe-area insets — is still unconfirmed on a device.
The dark theme is a real authored rendition and passes the contrast suite, but was only spot-checked visually.
deadTokens: --rule-heavy is declared in both themes and never referenced.
--focus is declared in both themes and never referenced; focus rings are drawn with a solid --secure outline instead.
verification.cascadeLayers: Tokens are unlayered on :root, element defaults are in @layer base, and the printed vocabulary is in @layer components so Tailwind utilities override it. This structure is load-bearing and must not be undone.

narrative.overview:
PairCode is an access-control system, so its interface is a credential and a reader — not a dashboard about security. The world is borrowed from secured document printing: safety-paper stock in a green-grey that no word processor produces by accident, one committed intaglio green for anything the server has actually decided, ruled hairlines instead of gaps, and issued cards carrying a portrait panel, a role band and a machine-readable strip. A reviewer landing cold should be able to tell within seconds that identity, permission and liveness are facts being printed onto an artifact, not decorations arranged around one.

The governing commitment is that every credential device on the surface encodes a real fact. A role band is the real role the server returned. An expiry is the real invite expiry. The MRZ strip is the real signed invite token, chevron-padded into fixed 30-character courses but never case-normalised, because the strip has to remain the payload. The guilloché rosette is a deterministic hypotrochoid derived from the identity's own id — a visual hash, so the same operator carries the same figure in every room on every device, and two operators cannot collide by accident. A cancellation stamp appears only where access has actually been revoked. Ornament that means nothing is out of system and should be deleted rather than restyled.

The density is high and deliberately clerical: a fixed-height three-column desk at desktop, columns that scroll inside themselves, near-zero decorative whitespace. What the world refuses is the elevated-card grid every collaboration tool ships — floating rounded panels on a neutral page, separated by shadow and air. Here separation is done with a 1px rule and a tonal shift in the stock, and lift is reserved for the two things that are physically loose objects. The build ships one authored moment of motion: the reader sweep that crosses a panel while the room agent is actually streaming.
keyCharacteristics: Safety-paper green-grey stock, never cream and never pure white
One committed colour (intaglio green) plus two exception colours that appear only when their fact is true
Archivo condensed caps for printed legends, Courier Prime for machine-typed values — two voices, never blended
Hairline rules and banded stock in place of gaps and shadows
Square 2px corners everywhere; the 12px ID-1 corner belongs to issued credentials alone
Every device on the surface is decodable from a legend printed on the same page

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Intaglio green is the system's only committed colour. Ochre and vermilion are not accents available for emphasis — each is bound to one condition (a live guest session; an actual revocation or refusal). If a new panel wants a third colour to make something stand out, the answer is a rule, a band, or a legend, not a new hue.

rules.name: The Never-By-Eye Rule
rules.body: lib/theme-contrast.test.ts parses the token values straight out of app/globals.css and asserts 4.5:1 in both themes for every foreground/background pair that ships text — there is no shipped text pair the suite does not cover — plus 3:1 for the lamp against the sheet. Retuning a colour because it looked better on your monitor will fail the suite before it ships. Change a token, run bun test, and if a pair fails, move the token — do not relax the pair. A new coloured surface that carries text arrives with its own themed ink token and its own asserted pair; that is what keeps this rule true.

rules.name: The Fact-Bound Ink Rule
rules.body: A colour on this surface is a claim. Green means the server committed; ochre means provisional and short-lived; vermilion means refused or revoked. Never reach for one because a control needed to look important.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: If a human or a designer wrote it, it is Archivo. If a machine produced it — an id, a token, a code, a timestamp, a path, a count — it is Courier Prime via .value. There is no third voice, and no mixing inside one string.

rules.name: The Sentence Is Never Tracked Rule
rules.body: Tracked caps are for fixed printed legends of one to three words. A full sentence goes in .note or body, in sentence case. A legend that has grown into a sentence is a .note that was mislabelled.

rules.name: The Mark Step Rule
rules.body: 0.5625rem is a mark, not a size. It is available only for a word stamped onto an object or an initial set inside a credential mark, where the reader decodes a symbol rather than reads a line. Anything a person actually reads — a label, a caption, a divider, a hint — starts at the 0.625rem legend and goes up. If you are reaching for the mark step to fit more text into a space, the answer is less text or a bigger space.

rules.name: The Payload Is Not Copy Rule
rules.body: Strings that are real payloads — the invite token in the MRZ, a socket id, a user id — are never case-normalised, prettified, or truncated for looks. Pad and wrap them; do not edit them.

rules.name: The Ruled Course Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by a 1px rule and a tonal shift in the stock, not by a gap plus a shadow. A new panel joins the desk by adopting .sheet and a .sheet-head; it does not float beside the others.

rules.name: The Internal Scroll Rule
rules.body: At lg the shell owns the viewport height and every column scrolls in place. A new panel must survive min-h-0 inside a flex column — give it flex min-h-0 flex-col and put the scroll on its own content, never on the page.

rules.name: The Only Credentials Lift Rule
rules.body: If a surface is not an issued credential or a genuinely floating overlay, it gets a border and a tonal step, never a shadow. A new sheet carrying a box-shadow has left the world.

rules.name: The Contact Line Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in this system opens with a 1px zero-blur line before its soft drop. A single soft blur alone reads as a web card, not as paper on paper.

rules.name: The ID-1 Corner Rule
rules.body: 12px belongs to issued credentials. Everything else on the surface is 2px. If you find yourself wanting a rounded panel, you are building a card in a world that has no cards — build a .sheet.

dos: Do make every credential device encode a real fact. A band is a real role; an expiry is the real expiry; an MRZ strip is a real signed token; a guilloché is a hash of a real id; a stamp means access was actually revoked. If you cannot bind a device to a fact, delete it.
Do build a new panel as a .sheet with a .sheet-head — square 2px, 1px rule border, stock-face ground, flat, intaglio head carrying a legend-lg title.
Do keep the vocabulary in @layer components and the tokens unlayered, so Tailwind utilities keep overriding the vocabulary. Do not restructure the layers in app/globals.css.
Do run bun test after touching any colour. lib/theme-contrast.test.ts reads the tokens straight out of the stylesheet and asserts 4.5:1 in both themes.
Do print a legend for any new mark you introduce. The rack's "Key to the marks" is held level with the rack it explains; a device the reader cannot decode from the same page does not ship.
Do carry state in a word as well as in a colour or a shape — Visitor, Away, Revoked, Machine issued, connected.
Do show owner-only controls in their real disabled state under .overprint with a reason, rather than hiding them.
Do set machine-produced strings in .value (Courier Prime, tabular figures), and zero-pad counts.
Do author both themes when you add a token. Dark is a real rendition of the same door, not a filter.
donts: Don't put a 12px radius on anything that is not an issued credential, and don't introduce a third radius. 2px everywhere, 12px for .credential, 9999px for the lamp dot.
Don't add a box-shadow to a sheet, a row, a field, or a badge. Only credentials and genuinely floating overlays lift, and both shadows open with a 1px contact line.

Don't introduce a fourth colour. If something needs emphasis, use a rule, a band, a legend, or a tonal step in the stock. Ochre and vermilion are bound to guest sessions and to revocation or refusal respectively.
Don't set a sentence in tracked caps, or a person's name in the legend voice. .legend is for one-to-three-word printed labels.
Don't case-normalise, prettify, or truncate a real payload for the sake of the layout. Pad and wrap it.
Don't seed a guilloché with anything but a stable real identity. No random seeds, no list indices, no display names.
Don't separate panels with air and elevation. This world separates with a hairline and a tonal shift.
Don't print text onto a coloured field with a literal colour. A coloured field gets a themed ink token — secure-ink, provisional-ink — and an asserted contrast pair alongside it.
Don't claim the mobile layout works. It is authored but has never been captured; verify it before you rely on it.
